findings.asked: Total surface area of a solid made of two cylinders stacked.
findings.wentWrong: Only the strongest finished; errors included finding volume, forgetting to subtract the small circle where the cylinders meet, and using the wrong curved-surface formula. Examiners asked for work laid out with each calculation named.
findings.fullMarkAnswersDid: Listed the external faces: two curved surfaces, the top circle, the bottom circle, and the ring (large circle minus small circle) where they join.
findings.rule: Count only surfaces that touch the air, and label each one.

findings.asked: The same compound surface area on M3.
findings.wentWrong: Many totalled the complete surface areas of both cylinders; others could not see the middle ring as a difference of circles; a large number calculated volumes instead.
findings.rule: The contact ring is the difference of two circles.

findings.asked: Find a cone's radius from the volume of a frustum-like difference of cones.
findings.wentWrong: Almost nobody finished: the subtraction of volumes was set up by some, but 3r was squared without brackets and the simplification failed.
findings.rule: Bracket (3r) before squaring; simplify each term separately.

ruleToRemember: List the external faces of a compound solid one by one (the contact ring is a difference of two circles), label each calculation, and bracket scaled radii before squaring.
aStarSignal: A frustum or stacked-solid problem set up as an equation in an unknown radius and solved without bracket errors.
